canonical.meaning: durable product or lifecycle truth; only domain-approved commits may mutate it

cache.meaning: derived or coordination state that may be discarded and rebuilt

log.meaning: append-only evidence that is never read as current product truth

canonical.commit.deletion: tombstone record with a JSON null value

cache.replace.scope: one community, one cache record type, and one source checkpoint
cache.replace.replacementTarget: recordType is mandatory even when the replacement writes are empty
cache.replace.commit: replace the supplied cache set atomically

log.append.commit: append all entries atomically or none

queryIntents.by_key: one exact typed record in one community
queryIntents.page: one typed record class in one community with a bounded cursor page
queryIntents.changes: all canonical record types, ordered after a canonical sequence; recordType and key are empty

projectionRebuild.publishRule: replace only when input identity and output identity match exactly

invariants: community scope is mandatory and adapter-derived
a transaction never mixes canonical, cache, and log records
a transaction contains each typed key at most once
cache and log records cannot become canonical truth
queries are typed intents rather than SQL or arbitrary filter strings
projection rows are replaceable and reproducible from canonical input
no compatibility mode, legacy runtime fallback, or Chirps domain ownership
